providers.name: Groq
providers.desc: The speed king. Groq's LPU hardware pushes Llama 3.1 8B at around 1,000 tokens per second. Fast enough for real-time apps. Good for batch work too: 14,400 requests per day on the free tier.
steps: Head to console.groq.com
Create an account (free, no card)
Grab your API key. Takes about 10 seconds.
Paste it into any OpenAI-compatible app, or use ChatUI, LibreChat, or Open WebUI
providers.note: Great for: high-volume annotation, real-time chat, speech-to-text. The speed advantage is real. It genuinely feels snappier than most local setups.

providers.name: OpenRouter
providers.desc: Access 27+ models through one standardized API. It also handles automatic failover. If one model hits rate limits, it routes to another. Best for benchmarking and finding the right model for your task.
steps: Go to openrouter.ai and sign up
Navigate to Keys → Create new key
Check the free models filter under Models to see what's available
Use with any OpenAI-compatible client
providers.note: Use `openrouter/free` as your fallback endpoint. It auto-routes to whatever free model is available when others hit limits. 20 requests/min, 200/day.

providers.name: Google AI Studio
providers.desc: Gemini 2.5 Flash is the workhorse here. Native search grounding (it can check facts against Google), Python code execution, 1 million token context window, and solid multimodal support. 1,500 requests per day free.
steps: Visit aistudio.google.com
Sign in with any Google account
Go to API keys → Create API key
Integrate with any Gemini-compatible app
providers.note: Best for: long documents, data science, hallucination checking (search grounding is genuinely useful), and nuanced evaluation work. Gemini 2.5 Pro has a tighter limit but better reasoning.

providers.name: Cerebras
providers.desc: Wafer-scale hardware. This is where you go when you need raw throughput. GPT OSS 120B hits around 3,000 tokens per second. Llama 3.1 8B sits at 2,600+ TPS. No other free service comes close on sheer speed.
steps: Go to cerebras.ai and create an account
Navigate to API → Get API key
Use their SDK or any OpenAI-compatible client
Start with Llama 3.1 8B for the fastest responses
providers.note: For batch annotation. You can process 50,000 audits in minutes. This is the platform to use when Groq's speed still isn't fast enough and you're processing large volumes.

providers.name: SiliconFlow
providers.desc: 200+ models under one roof, and a $1 free credit to start. The standout is Nex-N2-Pro at effectively $0 per million tokens on the free tier. Supports image and video generation too, like HunyuanVideo, FLUX.1, and Wan2.2.
steps: Sign up at siliconflow.com
Get $1 free credit on signup
Browse models and filter by cost to find the free ones
API is OpenAI-compatible, works with most clients
providers.note: Best for: long-context batch processing, image generation, and video. The $1 credit goes a long way when using the free-tier models. No credit card needed to start.

providers.name: Ollama Cloud
providers.desc: Runs Ollama's model library on cloud GPUs. Same command-line interface you use locally, just with more horsepower. Good for long-horizon agentic tasks that need 1M token context beyond what your local machine can handle.
steps: Install Ollama locally from ollama.com
Sign up for Ollama Cloud at cloud.ollama.com
Run cloud models with the same ollama run command
Use custom modelfiles to point to cloud endpoints
providers.note: The magic here is consistency. If you're already using Ollama locally, the cloud version feels identical. Sessions reset every ~5 hours, so don't expect long-running state.

providers.name: Hugging Face Spaces
providers.desc: Browser-based AI apps. No API key needed for most. Thousands of apps covering chatbots, image generation, coding assistants, audio processing, and more. Hit or miss on quality, but completely free for most.
steps: Go to huggingface.co/spaces
Browse by category or search for what you need
Click any space. Most run directly in your browser
Sign up only if you want to create your own spaces
providers.note: Best for: quick experiments, trying models without commitment, and exploring what's possible. Some popular spaces get slow during peak hours. No consistency guarantee.
